reviews.headline: Up 2.9% on day one, but it's all parked cash; 3 buy orders still waiting
reviews.markdown:
**Account:** $1,029.66 vs $1,000 start (+2.91% today and this week). The goal is +5%, so we're a little over halfway. The S&P buy-and-hold would be $1,009.40, so we're ahead by about $20. Be honest: no trade closed, so this gain is not from Patient Levels. It came from the account's moves in the market, and I can't tell you how much was luck.

**Core vs trading:** About $519 of idle cash was moved into the S&P (market order at 3:52pm, still pending). Settled cash is $30.91. No open positions, so no stops to report.

**Orders today (none filled yet):**
- TLN limit buys at $346.08 and $355.66. TLN closed near $365.61 (+9.8%), so both are sitting below the price. They only fill if it pulls back.
- BWXT limit buy at $115.83, with the stock at $115.86, so this one is very close.

**Agent decision:** BWXT jumped 6.7% on the Westinghouse AP1000 deal news. The desk took no action. That's right: news is priced in within minutes. Past BWXT deal headlines averaged -2.8% over the next 20 days. It's still down 51% from its 1-year high.

**Watch tomorrow:** whether the BWXT order fills, and whether TLN dips. TLN's insiders sold $23M over the year (COO sale on Nov 17). Nothing was bought, which is a mild caution.

**Lesson:** A good day isn't proof a strategy works. Patient Levels has only 1 data point so far, so judge it on many trades, not one.

reviews.headline: Down 1.24% today, but still +1.62% on the week and ahead of the S&P
reviews.markdown:
**Account:** $1,016.74 vs $1,000 start. Today -$12.92 (-1.24%). The week is +1.62%, short of the +5% goal (the goal isn't forced). The S&P buy-and-hold would be $1,004.23, so we're ahead by about $12.50, but we lost to the S&P today (-1.24% vs -0.48%).

**Why we fell:** Nuclear stocks dropped 2.49% as a group. Our "panic" holdings took the hits: LEU -4.94, VST -4.15, UUUU -2.13 (in the day's attribution), and the parked SPY -2.16. No Patient Levels trades were open, armed or waiting, and none closed today.

**Orders (all 15:40, still pending):**
- Sold $71 of parked SPY to fund a trade. This created a small wash-sale flag: a -$0.61 loss that is deferred, not lost.
- Three "sharp-drop rebound" buys: AMD, NNE, SMR.
- Ten "thanksgiving" buys, one in each lineup stock.

**Concerns:**
- The account shows cash of -$352.92 and settled cash of $0. With no margin allowed, 13 market buys pending on that is a red flag. The Account Officer and Risk Manager should confirm what will actually fill.
- The basket is below its 10-day average, so normal new buys should be blocked. These orders come from other rules, so someone should check that is intended.

**Red day verdict:** This looks like the cost of holding in a falling market (the S&P is below its 200-day average), not a broken rule. The cash question above is the possible fix. We shouldn't change any rule over one day.

**Watch tomorrow:** which orders fill and at what size, the cash balance, and UUUU (down 68% in a quarter, with law-firm "investigation" notices out). Those notices are noise, but they add to the pressure on the stock.

desk_log.headline: Cameco (TSX:CCO) On Its Loss And Share Sale With Fair Value Back In Focus

investigator.summary: The Yahoo/Simply Wall St piece is a recap of old facts. Cameco's Q3 (reported Oct 30) showed a C$2M adjusted loss after a longer Key Lake mill outage, and the US$1B at-the-market (ATM) share program was renewed and doubled in early December. The stock has since fallen about 25% in 20 days, partly on a sector-wide selloff in AI-linked nuclear names, so the news is already priced in.
investigator.key_risk: The ATM lets Cameco sell new shares into any bounce, which can cap rallies. A further sector slide would also hit CCJ, since it is below its 10-day, 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages and the basket is falling. The other risk is a sharp oversold bounce (RSI2 of 0.58) that stops out a patient buy. The next real catalyst is Q4 results and the 2027 production plan in February, and I couldn't confirm an exact date.
investigator.say: To News Scout: thanks for flagging it, but I'd call this priced in. The Q3 loss and the share-sale program were reported weeks ago, and the stock has already dropped about 25% in 20 days, with much of the recent fall coming with no new Cameco news, just the AI-nuclear sector selling off. The share sale (which dilutes existing owners) is a real overhang, but the stock is far below its averages and the basket is falling, so I say no new buy for now and wait for a base to form.

CCJ.reason: The news is a recap of old facts (Q3 loss, share-sale program) and is already priced in, so it gives us no edge. CCJ is below all its major averages and the whole basket is falling, which breaks our no-new-buys rule, so we stay out.

pm.plan_summary: No position and nothing waiting in CCJ, so nothing to cancel or sell. I'm skipping: stale news, a falling basket, and a stock down about 25% in 20 days with no base yet. I'd revisit once the basket is back above its 10-day average and CCJ shows a stable support level; the February Q4 results are the next real catalyst, but the exact date is unconfirmed.
pm.say: I agree with the News Investigator: this is a recap of old news (Q3 loss, share-sale program) that the market already absorbed, so there's no edge. Also, CCJ is deeply oversold (down about 25% in 20 days), but 'cheap' isn't a reason to buy while the whole basket is falling, and our rules say no new buys then. I'm skipping and waiting for a base to form.

desk_log.headline: BWXT stock surges on Westinghouse AP1000 manufacturing deal By Investing.com - Investing.com Australia

investigator.summary: Westinghouse Canada gave BWXT Canada manufacturing qualification contracts for AP1000 reactor components. These are qualification contracts, meaning BWXT is being approved to make parts, not receiving large production orders, and the stock is up about 7% today on volume at only 0.21x its 20-day average.
investigator.key_risk: The 7% pop is a bounce inside a downtrend (below the 20, 50 and 200-day averages, down 11% over 20 days). Qualification contracts have no stated dollar value, and the desk's history shows BWXT's contract-deal news fades over the next 20 days (median -2.8%, up only 40% of the time).
investigator.say: News Scout, thanks for flagging this. I'd call it mostly priced in: the contracts only qualify BWXT to make AP1000 parts, with no disclosed dollar value, and the stock already jumped 7% today. The desk's own history shows BWXT's past contract news usually faded over the next 20 days, and the price is still below its 50-day average, so I'd wait for a patient limit-buy near support rather than chase.

BWXT.reason: The AP1000 qualification contracts have no disclosed dollar value, and the stock already jumped 7% today. BWXT is still in a downtrend, and its past contract news faded over 20 days (median -2.8%, up only 40% of the time), so I see no specific reason to buy now.

pm.plan_summary: No trade in BWXT. A 7% bounce on unquantified qualification contracts inside a downtrend is chasing, not a patient entry. Revisit only if the stock pulls back to a real support level.
pm.say: I agree with the News Investigator that this is priced in: the contracts only approve BWXT to make AP1000 parts, with no dollar value attached, and the stock already rose 7%. The desk's history says BWXT contract news tends to fade over the next 20 days, and the stock is below its 20, 50 and 200-day averages, so I'm skipping rather than chasing the pop.

msgs.text: Test: trades where group_up == False (5437 of 9820). Older half: 0.128R vs 0.481R for the rest. Newer half: 0.132R vs 0.214R. p=0.0. Verdict: not supported.
Test: trades where ret5d_pct > 10 (457 of 9820). Older half: 0.1R vs 0.316R for the rest. Newer half: 0.091R vs 0.167R. p=0.1605. Verdict: not supported.

Risk Manager here, and I disagree with the 'not supported' verdicts being read as a clean no: both ideas were tested after seeing the data, and the group_up result is a big p=0.0 result that actually points the opposite way from the claim. Five ideas tested so far means some of these could be luck, and the desk's own history shows the 'worse after big run-ups' pattern is already noisy. I'd log both as tested and rejected, not build rules from them, and I'd keep the research pipeline honest about trial counts before trusting any new pattern.
msgs.notes:
why: group_up==False trades averaged clearly better in the older half and still better in the newer half, which contradicts the claim that they should do worse; the ret5d_pct result is weak (p=0.16) and reverses only slightly across halves. With 5 ideas tested, the multiple-comparison risk is real, so neither result justifies a new rule.

research_log.name: panic_day_rebound
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. research_log.name: support_vs_dipbuy_fills
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-23 (10 nuclear stocks, Dec 2023-Nov 2026 hourly for support buys, daily for the dip-buy; $1,000, 25% per trade, max 4 open). questions.question: TLN closed around $364 after a 9% day, yet the resting buy sits at $355.66 with a $354.24 support zone. Is this order still a deliberate plan, or should it be canceled now that the stock has moved well away from it?
questions.answer: The resting buy at $355.66 was a plan for a dip toward the $354.24 support, and TLN now trades about 2.4% above it after a 9% sector bounce, which our rules say not to chase. The basket is still below its 10-day average, which blocks new buys, so this order should not be left resting into a bounce. I agree with the Risk Manager's concern that a sharp reversal could fill it, and I'd cancel it rather than let it sit until the PJM capacity-auction delay is decided.

questions.question: Has the PJM December capacity-auction delay been decided? The Talen headline calls the long-term sales a 'pullback opportunity', but the earnings driver is still an open regulatory question.
questions.answer: I checked the desk files and the headlines we have for PJM. Nothing I can see shows the December capacity-auction delay has been decided; the only mention is the Talen 'pullback opportunity' article, which doesn't report a regulator decision. Since the earnings driver is still pending, I'd treat the 9% jump as pricing in an unresolved outcome, and I agree with the Risk Manager that the resting TLN buy shouldn't be left in place into this bounce.

questions.question: BWXT rallied 7.4% on the AP1000 demonstration-parts headline, but the price is still down about 8% on the month and 15% below its 20-day high. Does the $115.37 support zone mean anything after a news-driven spike, or is it just where the price happened to be before the pop?
questions.answer: The $115.37 zone was drawn before the news pop, and the price has since run 7.4% above the zone's level, so it's a stale level, not a fresh floor. Nothing in the desk's notes shows support forming after the headline, and the basket is still below its 10-day average, so no new buys are allowed anyway. I agree with the Risk Manager that the basket rule should block this, and I'd treat the BWXT setup as stale until the price actually retests a zone drawn from after the bounce.

questions.question: The AP1000 headline has no disclosed contract value, so is this news big enough to change BWXT's revenue outlook, or is it a small qualification step that the market is overpricing?
questions.answer: The AP1000 headline is a qualification step with no disclosed dollar value, and BWXT's own history shows contract-news pops tend to fade over 20 days (median -2.8%), so I don't think it changes the revenue outlook. I agree with the Level Analyst that the $115.37 zone predates the bounce and is stale, and the basket is below its 10-day average, so no new buy either way.

questions.question: TLN closed near $364, roughly 2.4% above the resting buy at $355.66, and the basket is still down about 6% versus its 10-day average. Is this order still a deliberate plan, or is it a leftover that should be canceled given the no-new-buys rule?
questions.answer: I'm answering the Questioner's question directly: this resting buy at $355.66 is a leftover, not a deliberate plan. The basket is still about 6-7.5% below its 10-day average, our rule blocks new buys in that condition, and TLN has already run about 2.4-3.8% above the entry, so the order would only fill on a further sector drop. I agree with the Questioner that it should be canceled, and I'd say the same thing on any setup that gets canceled under the rule.

questions.question: TLN's COO Brad Berryman sold about $19.8M of stock on Nov 17 at roughly $345-365. Was that a planned 10b5-1 sale or an open-market sale?
questions.answer: I checked the desk files on TLN's Nov 17 COO sale: about $19.8M at $345-365, and the files tag it as an open-market sale, not a planned 10b5-1 one, so the planned-versus-open-market question has a clear answer. That makes it a real warning sign, though one insider sale alone is weak evidence since TLN's insiders have been net sellers over 12 months anyway. I agree with the Risk Manager that the $355.66 resting buy should be canceled today unless someone re-approves it in writing.

questions.question: Who explicitly owns the TLN resting buy at $355.66 right now? The basket is below its 10-day average, so the no-new-buys rule applies. If nobody re-approves it in writing, should it be canceled today?

policy.item: US ban on Russian enriched uranium
policy.status: In force since Aug 11 2024 and lasts until the end of 2040. Waivers (exceptions) are only allowed until Jan 1 2028.
policy.why: Russia supplied about a fifth of the enriched uranium US reactors use. From 2028 that has to come from somewhere else.

policy.status: Centrus has waivers for all deliveries already promised to US customers in 2026 and 2027. Well over half of what it delivers through 2027 comes from Russia's Tenex.
policy.why: 2028 cuts both ways for Centrus: its cheap Russian supply ends, but demand for US-made enrichment rises.

policy.status: Since Nov 2024 Tenex needs a separate Russian export licence for each shipment to the US; extended through Dec 31 2027.
policy.why: Russia can stop shipments early at any time, which would hit Centrus before 2028.

LEU.summary: This is Centrus's Q3 2026 results release, and it's a mixed bag: GAAP net income of $31.6M looks strong, but it's driven by a one-time $46.4M non-cash warrant gain, while adjusted results show a $9.4M loss and revenue fell 26%. The bigger worries are that DOE's proposed FY2027 budget drops funding for the HALEU cascade (about $0.8B of backlog) and DOE won't exercise further options, which is a real hit to the Technical Solutions business. I'm not buying into this on the headline; I'd rather see how the Piketon lease and DOE funding play out.
